title: About A/B testing for Meta Ads

facts.fact: Meta describes A/B testing as comparing two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement, with each version shown to a segment of the audience so nobody sees both.
facts.quote: Each version is shown to a segment of your audience, ensuring nobody sees both, then the test determines which version performs best.

facts.fact: When an A/B test is created by duplicating an existing campaign, the campaign's ad budget is also duplicated.
facts.quote: If you choose to duplicate an existing campaign, your ad budget is also duplicated.

facts.fact: When an A/B test compares existing campaigns or ad sets rather than duplicating one, the current ad budgets are used and can be changed in Meta Ads Manager at the ad set level.
facts.quote: Otherwise, your current ad budgets are used, which you can change in Meta Ads Manager at the ad set level.

facts.fact: Meta recommends using the same budget for both versions in an A/B test to ensure a fair comparison.
facts.quote: Use the same budget for both versions in a test to ensure a fair comparison.

facts.fact: Meta states that A/B testing can measure each strategy's performance on a cost per result basis or a cost per conversion lift basis.
facts.quote: A/B testing can then measure the performance of each strategy on a cost per result basis or cost per conversion lift basis.

facts.fact: Meta does not recommend informal testing, such as manually turning ad sets or campaigns on and off.
facts.quote: We do not recommend testing informally, such as by turning ad sets or campaigns on and off manually.

facts.fact: Meta says informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results, and that A/B testing helps keep audiences evenly split and statistically comparable instead of overlapping.
facts.quote: Informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results.
